summary: Ship. The removal does what was asked: the writer, the two tests and the CONVENTIONS mention are gone. All hooks still fail open, including with an injected exception and with docs/compound-v/runs being a file, and no hook recreates triage.log. Core tests (164), hook wrapper/band/onboard/skills tests, frontmatter lint and shellcheck pass, and core is 2490 lines. One low edge remains: if a user committed the leftover log and deletes it during an open run, scope flags the deletion.

findings.title: Deleting a committed leftover triage.log during an open run is a scope violation
findings.evidence: scripts/cvcore/snapshot.py:38-42 unhashed() excludes evidence names only while the file exists on disk, and scope.py:14 builds its excludes from that list. In probe 2 (committed case), after `git commit` of docs/compound-v/runs/triage.log and `rm` of it inside a run, `compound-v.py scope` lists docs/compound-v/runs/triage.log under changed and violations. When the log is untracked (the common case, and how this repo has it via *.log in .gitignore), nothing is flagged. Before this change the prompt hook recreated the file at once, so a deletion rarely stuck. Now deleting the log is the natural cleanup.
findings.reproduce: cd CHECKOUT && python3 -I -B .review-probes/probe2.py | grep 'committed] scope after log delete'
findings.recommendation: Always exclude the literal path docs/compound-v/runs/triage.log in scope, present or not, or add a release note telling users to delete it outside an open run.
